sections.h2: What the Montgomery County Register of Deeds handles
sections.html:
This office keeps the paper trail of land ownership in the county: deeds, deeds of trust, easements, plats, releases and the index that ties them together. The county's department page calls it the legal custodian of real estate and vital records.

Staff also handle military discharge records (DD 214), assumed name and partnership filings, and UCC fixture filings. Residents come for marriage licenses and certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates, and newly commissioned notaries take their oath there.

A seller in Troy, Biscoe, Candor, Star or Mount Gilead meets this office at the very end of a sale. A buyer's title examiner searches its index before closing, and the new deed lands in its books afterward. A quick cash sale follows the same route as any other.

Montgomery County is a small, rural county in the Uwharrie region, with an estimated 26,403 people in mid-2025 spread over 491.54 square miles of land, roughly 52 residents per square mile. Housing units number 15,439. Owners live in 75.0 percent of households, the typical home was valued at $161,700 for 2020 to 2024, and typical rent was $766. Builders took out 176 permits in 2025.

Sellers here include long-time owners, older owners and heirs, and each of them relies on a deed that was recorded correctly.

sections.h2: Who owes the excise tax at closing?
sections.html:
The seller. Under the statute, whoever transfers the property hands the tax to the county's land records office ahead of recording (G.S. 105-228.30).

The levy is $1.00 on each $500 block of value, and a partial block counts as a whole one. Half of every payment stays with the county and the other half goes to the State.

  • Your closing attorney normally carries the payment in with the deed.
  • If a parcel spans two counties, the county with more of its value collects.
  • Ask the attorney for the final amount before signing, since it tracks the value stated on the deed.

The county has no price list of its own. G.S. 161-10 sets a single schedule for every register of deeds, calls it complete and exclusive, and requires payment before filing.

  • An ordinary deed is priced by page count, with a flat charge for the opening pages and a smaller one for each sheet after those.
  • A mortgage or deed of trust costs more than a deed, with a longer first stretch of pages.
  • Plats are priced per sheet and certified copies per page.
  • Filing the lender's release after payoff is free.
  • A page that breaks the state formatting rules picks up its own add-on charge.

Read the statute for the exact dollar figures. When a payoff is part of your sale, the free release means the lender's cleanup step costs you nothing extra.

sections.h2: How the tax office uses what is recorded
sections.html:
The Tax Administrator keeps the ownership and parcel records that begin with recorded deeds, then lists, values and bills each property. The county tax department oversees about 30,000 parcels of real property.

Which office sends your bill depends on the address. The county collects its own tax plus the real estate tax for Biscoe, Star, Candor and Mount Gilead. Troy collects for itself. Lake Tillery, Badin Lake and Wadeville fire district charges ride along on the county bill.

  • The county was last revalued in 2020, with the next reappraisal scheduled for 2028.
  • Commissioners set the rate in June, and the county mails bills in the summer after that.
  • Bills fall due September 1 and are not past due until January 5.
  • The listing window runs from January 2 to January 31, and listing late costs a 10% penalty.
  • To collect unpaid tax the office can garnish wages, attach bank accounts, levy personal property, use debt setoff or foreclose on real estate.

The state tax lien reaches the parcel on the listing date (G.S. 105-355), so request a payoff statement from the tax office or Troy before any fall or winter closing.

sections.h2: What if a signed deed is left unrecorded?
sections.html:
A buyer holding an unrecorded deed is exposed. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance, an option or a lease running past three years gives no protection against lien creditors, or buyers who paid value, until it is entered in the land records of the parcel's own county.

Registration order sets priority. If a creditor records a judgment before the deed is filed, the creditor may win. Families sometimes keep a signed deed in a drawer for years, and that habit is the surest way to create the problem.

The cure is quick. Carry the signed, notarized deed in along with the excise payment and filing fee, and keep the recording details the staff hand back.

Most of the effort comes before anyone reaches the counter. Register of deeds staff in North Carolina record documents without drafting them or advising on them, so a lawyer prepares the deed.

  • Look up the parcel number and owner record on the county's real estate and GIS search so the deed's description matches the tax record.
  • Gather payoff letters for each mortgage or lien, and confirm each lender will file its release.
  • Find out whether the county or the Town of Troy collects the tax on your parcel.
  • Have the excise payment and the recording fee ready as separate amounts.
  • Keep the notarized original with the recording stamp once the deed is filed.

Call the Montgomery County Register of Deeds for current hours and ask how it accepts documents before you make the trip. If your attorney is filing for you, ask who will bring the paper in and who will confirm the recording afterward, so nothing sits on a desk over a weekend.

sections.h2: Other county offices that touch a home sale
sections.html:
The register of deeds is one stop among several. Each office below can come up during a sale.

Montgomery County offices and what they answer
OfficeTypical question
InspectionsUnpermitted work a buyer may spot
PlanningLot size and setbacks outside town limits
Environmental HealthWell and septic questions on rural lots
Public UtilitiesMoving the water account to the buyer
Tax DepartmentParcel records, values, bills and payoffs

The county also runs a program to enroll farmland in a voluntary agricultural district, and an enrolled parcel carries that status into the sale. Its website has a how-do-I menu with a real estate and GIS search, a permit link and an occupancy tax payment link. Starting there often saves a phone call.

faqs.q: Which party owes the Montgomery County excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. The transferor pays the county office ahead of filing, at $1.00 per $500 block of value.

faqs.q: Where is the price list for recording in Montgomery County?
faqs.a: G.S. 161-10 is the one price list every North Carolina register of deeds follows. Pages drive the charge for a deed, a mortgage costs more, and a release after payoff is free.

faqs.q: Will the office draft my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. Staff file deeds but do not write them or offer legal advice. A closing attorney or other lawyer prepares the deed, and the office records it after it is signed and notarized.

faqs.q: When is a Montgomery County tax bill late?
faqs.a: September 1 is the due date, and January 5 is the point where a bill is past due. Interest then starts at 2%, and each month from February adds another 3/4 of 1%.

faqs.q: Does the county collect tax on a house inside Troy?
faqs.a: Troy collects its own real estate tax. The county office handles the county bill plus the bills for Biscoe, Star, Candor and Mount Gilead, so a Troy owner can expect a town bill and a county bill.
